---
order: 4
unit: drawing
introduces: [loop-index]
title: Use the counter
summary: The loop counter i changes every pass, so a line can grow without you typing each number.
language: python
hook: "Progress bars, animation frames and game levels all count. The loop counter is how code counts."
app:
  command: "node \"$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs\" \"$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground\" 8123"
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8123/index.html"
  ready: Python code
  layout: full
voice: true
explainClip:
  query: { code: "", speed: 8 }
  caption: "The counter i changes every pass"
  say: "The counter i is a different number on every pass."
  pacing: { keyDelayMs: 22 }
  clip:
    - type: { into: "Python code", text: "from turtle import *\n\nfor i in range(30):\n", append: true }
    - caption:
        text: "i is 0 on the first pass, 1 on the second, and so on."
        say: "i is zero on the first pass, one on the second."
    - type: { into: "Python code", text: "    forward(i * 5)\n    right(90)\n", append: true }
    - click: "Run"
    - caption:
        text: "Each line is longer than the last, so it spirals out."
        say: "Each line is longer than the last, so it spirals out."
    - wait: 1200
    - expect: { selector: "#status", contains: "Finished" }
---
You have met `i` in every loop so far, but never used it. It is a counter, and it changes on every pass.

## Predict

```step
stage: predict
code: counter.py#spiral
check:
  type: predict
  q: "What will the turtle draw?"
  options: ["a square", "a spiral that grows outward", "a circle", "nothing: i is never stored"]
  fault: logic
  misconception: counter-constant
  actual: "A spiral. i is 0 on the first pass, 1 on the second, 2 on the third, so i * 5 is 0, 5, 10, and every line is longer than the last."
```

This time `forward(i * 5)` uses the counter to work out how far to go. What do you think the turtle will draw?

## Run

```step
stage: run
code: counter.py#spiral
try: { starter: "counter.py#spiral", height: 420 }
```

Run it and compare it with your prediction.

Here is what each line does.

| Line | What it does | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `for i in range(30):` | Runs 30 times and makes a counter called `i` | `i` is 0 on the first pass, 1 on the second, up to 29 |
| `    forward(i * 5)` | Draws a line `i * 5` long | The lines are 0, 5, 10, 15 and so on, so they grow |
| `    right(90)` | Turns a quarter turn | The same turn every pass |

The first line is 0 steps long, because `i` is 0 on the first pass. Counting starts at 0, not 1.

## Investigate

```step
stage: investigate
code: counter.py#spiral
insight: "The counter takes a new value on every pass, so any line that uses it does something different each time round."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: trace
      text: "Fill in the counter and the length of the line on each pass."
      table: |
        | pass | i | line length (i * 5) |
        | 1 | 0 | 0 |
        | 2 | [1] | [5] |
        | 3 | [2] | [10] |
        | 4 | [3] | [15] |
      explain: "i starts at 0 and goes up by 1 each pass, so i * 5 goes 0, 5, 10, 15. The first line is 0 long, so you never see it."
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "A program has sides = 8 and turns right(360 / sides) on every pass of its loop. How many degrees is each turn?"
      answer: 45
      explain: "360 / 8 = 45. The name sides holds 8 each time the line runs."
```

Follow the counter round the loop, then use what you know about names.

### Follow the counter

Work out `i` and the length of the line on each pass.

### Work out the turn

A name holds a value you can calculate with.

## Modify

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Because the line length is worked out from i, changing one number changes every line of the spiral."
try: { starter: "counter.py#modify", height: 420 }
tasks:
  - hint: "Only one number needs to change. Which number is multiplied by i?"
    check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed one number so the spiral grows faster." }
  - hint:
      - "pensize( ) sets how thick the line is. The pen needs a number that changes each pass."
      - "The counter changes each pass, so use it. pensize(i + 1) starts at 1."
    check: { type: code, text: "Use the counter to change the pen size.", rules: { uses: [pensize] } }
    unlocks: [counter-step]
```

### Grow faster

Change one number so the spiral grows faster.

### Thicker and thicker

Use the counter to make the line thicker on every pass.

```teacher
summary: Students use the loop counter i to work out something different on
  every pass, and meet the fact that counting starts at 0.
time: 30
timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 12 min
goals:
  - I can say what i holds on each pass of a loop.
  - I can use i in a calculation inside a loop.
  - I can change a drawing by changing one number in that calculation.
before: >
  Run the spiral, then try pensize(i + 1) yourself. Notice the first line is
  invisible because i is 0.
running:
  - "Predict: show the loop with forward(i * 5) and ask what it draws. Take a
    vote before anyone runs it; the wrong options are a square (the counter does
    not change), a circle, and an error because i was never stored."
  - "Run: students run it and compare. Ask: how long is the first line, and why?"
  - "Investigate: trace the counter 0, 1, 2, 3 and say that counting starts at
    0, because later lessons rely on it. The second task checks that a name
    still holds a value you can calculate with."
  - "Modify: students change the multiplier, then use the counter for the pen.
    Let them try pensize(i) first: it starts at 0, so the first line is thin.
    That is a good moment to talk about starting at 0."
stuck:
  - see: The spiral is a square, with every line the same length.
    ask: Is the length worked out from i, or typed as a number?
    fix: The length must use i, for example forward(i * 5).
  - see: A student expects the first line to be 5 long.
    ask: What is i on the very first pass?
    fix: i is 0 on the first pass, so i * 5 is 0. Counting starts at 0.
  - see: An error says i is not defined.
    ask: Is the line that uses i indented inside the for loop?
    fix: i only exists inside the loop. Indent the line under the for line.
stretch: Draw a spiral that turns 91 degrees instead of 90. What happens, and why?
support: Give the first three values of i * 5 and ask the student to continue
  the pattern before running.
leads: "Next lesson makes a value grow without the counter: a variable that adds
  to itself. Counters are used for scores, timers and animations. Class ideas: a
  spiral gallery with different multipliers."
exit:
  q: "In for i in range(5): forward(i * 10), what is the length of the third
    line?"
  a: 20. The third pass has i = 2, and 2 * 10 = 20.
explain: >
  A loop made with `for i in range(30):` keeps a **counter** called `i`. It is 0
  on the first pass, 1 on the second, 2 on the third, and so on up to 29.


  Any line inside the loop can use `i`. `forward(i * 5)` draws a line that is 0,
  then 5, then 10 steps long, so each one is longer than the last and the path
  spirals outward.
solutions:
  step-4#t1: counter.py#sol-faster
  step-4#t2: counter.py#sol-thick
struggle: Believing the counter is the same number every pass, or that it starts
  at 1. Ask what i is on the first pass.
class:
  activities:
    - at: start
      kind: info
      title: By the end of this lesson
      do: >
        Here is the finished program running. By the end of the lesson you will
        write one like it.
      notes: Run the finished example on the projector before anything else.
    - at: investigate
      title: Walk the counter
      minutes: 5
      do: >
        Four volunteers say i aloud as the loop runs, 0, 1, 2, 3, while the
        class says each line length.
      notes: Make the idea physical before it goes back to the screen.
```
files.counter.py:
# region: spiral
from turtle import *

for i in range(30):
    forward(i * 5)
    right(90)
# endregion

# region: modify
from turtle import *

for i in range(30):
    forward(i * 5)
    right(90)

# Change one number so the spiral grows faster.
# Then make the line thicker on every pass.
# endregion

# region: sol-faster
from turtle import *

for i in range(30):
    forward(i * 10)
    right(90)
# endregion

# region: sol-thick
from turtle import *

for i in range(30):
    pensize(i + 1)
    forward(i * 5)
    right(90)
# endregion
